findings.evidence: NormControl.lean:42-43 and NegOne/Norm.lean:63-64 are identical to MassFormula/Quadratic/PadicTwo.lean:77 `coe_two_integerRing_padicTwo` and CyclotomicEight/Basic.lean:112 `coe_base_ofNat_two`; no public lemma exists (grep for `map_ofNat (Subring.subtype 𝒪[ℚ_[2]])` returns only these private/inline copies), and Mathlib has no general `SubringClass` `coe_ofNat` simp lemma.
findings.fix: Hoist one public lemma for `((2 : 𝒪[ℚ_[2]]) : ℚ_[2]) = 2` into a common base module (e.g. alongside the `𝒪[ℚ_[2]]` setup imported by these files) and reuse it in NormControl.lean, NegOne/Norm.lean, and the existing copies, instead of adding new private restatements.
findings.issue: `private theorem coe_two_padicIntegerRing : ((2 : 𝒪[ℚ_[2]]) : ℚ_[2]) = 2 := map_ofNat (Subring.subtype 𝒪[ℚ_[2]]) 2` restates, verbatim (same statement and proof term), two existing private helpers: `coe_two_integerRing_padicTwo` and `coe_base_ofNat_two`. NegOne/Norm.lean:63 re-derives the same fact a third time as an inline `have hcoe`. This is the same clone the prior review flagged for DyadicSqrtTwo, now reappearing for ℚ_[2].

summary: The PR reuses the generic defect / norm-filtration / Hilbert-symbol / Eisenstein-basis / unramified-class machinery correctly and adds genuinely new worked examples. One duplication: it adds a fourth and fifth copy of the trivial helper `((2 : 𝒪[ℚ_[2]]) : ℚ_[2]) = 2`, which already exists privately in two other modules.
